scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a claim response that largely accepts well-being as the surest indicator while granting that achievements matter; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: We are quick to praise a nation for its famous artists, scientists, and leaders.
Some people claim that the surest indicator of a great nation is not these achievements but the general well-being of all its people.
I largely agree with this claim, though I believe achievements still play a part in true greatness.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why well-being is the surest sign

sentences.text: First, the well-being of all the people is indeed the surest sign of national greatness.
A nation can shine with achievement while most of its citizens live in hardship.
For example, a country famous for its art but full of hungry families has failed its basic duty.
This shows that achievements mean little if ordinary people do not share in the benefits.
Good health, education, and security reach everyone, while fame reaches only a few.
Any nation that lifts all its people has met its truest purpose.
To this extent, the claim rightly points to well-being as the surest measure.
Second, however, the achievements of a nation should not be dismissed entirely.
Great discoveries and works of art often raise the very well-being the claim values most.
Consider how new medicine lengthens ordinary lives or how great art enriches a whole people.
Such achievements are frequently a cause of well-being rather than a rival to it.
Countries that prize learning and creativity usually become healthier and more prosperous too.
Achievements can also unite a people and give them pride in who they are.
Well-being and achievement, then, are partners rather than opposites.
In conclusion, the well-being of all the people is the surest indicator of a great nation.
But achievements matter too, since they often raise that well-being and enrich the culture.
Greatness belongs to the nation whose achievements serve the well-being of every citizen.
